A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RLHF survey and provide readable text, equations, figures, and tables. The appendices are accounted for: v3 Appendix B relocates v2 Section 1.4, while Appendix A expands the LLM discussion.

before.justification: v2 presents literature synthesis, conceptual classifications, and summaries of theoretical guarantees. Empirical outcomes are attributed to cited studies; no original empirical study or data analysis is reported.

after.justification: v3 remains a literature survey. Its appendices add explanations and comparisons of prior surveys, while empirical findings remain attributed to other work.

M1.justification: The generic actor-critic RLHF procedure in Algorithm 1 is unchanged. The expanded DPO and LLM discussions explain existing methods rather than introduce or modify a proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Neither survey conducts training or evaluation on datasets or tasks. Newly discussed music generation and RewardBench expand the literature covered without adding tasks actually executed by this work.

E2.justification: Neither version benchmarks a proposed method against experimental baselines. The matched theoretical comparison tables retain their algorithm membership; newly cited methods such as SRPO are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: No experimental protocol executed by this work is added or revised. Appendix A documents practices from existing LLM studies without establishing changes to experiments, splits, metrics, model configurations, or training budgets.

E4.justification: No ablation, sensitivity, robustness, or case-study analysis conducted by this work is added or removed. New discussions of failure modes and benchmark challenges review and interpret prior work.

E5.justification: No repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance-reporting practices are added or changed. Ensemble uncertainty and theoretical confidence bounds remain descriptions of surveyed methods.

E6.justification: Section 3.2.1 reverses the reported Askell et al. (2021) finding: v2 says rankings perform better, whereas v3 says binary comparisons, including pairs extracted from rankings, perform better. Section 4.1.1 removes the Eberhard et al. (2022) variance-versus-recency finding, and Appendix A adds cited PPO-versus-direct-method findings. These changes concern results attributed to prior work.

T1.justification: Section 5.1.4 corrects Φ(x) = 1/2 to Φ(0) = 1/2, and Section 2.1 replaces sampling from a scalar reward function with deterministic equality. Section 6.3 adds the explicit DPO loss, Eq. 14, while the formal trajectory-segment definition is removed. Section 7's theoretical guarantees are retained.

C1.justification: The broad RLHF-survey contribution remains. v3 more explicitly qualifies its coverage: greatest depth in control and robotics, a dedicated but non-exhaustive LLM treatment, and a mainly 2017-2024 literature window with later publication updates.

C2.justification: Beyond v2's brief LLM bandit discussion, Appendix A substantially develops explanations of exploration, distribution shift, offline versus online learning, and conditions under which multi-turn interactions or tool use invalidate the simplified setting. Section 5.1.6 also adds a substantive critique of mean preference aggregation and connects it to social choice.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly documents prompt reuse, overlap, or separation between preference learning and policy training, semi-online feedback updates, and early stopping in cited LLM studies. This expands technical guidance; the supporting-library overview in Section 8.2 is retained, and no changed experiment or new implementation release is established.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands literature synthesis around social choice and pluralistic alignment in Section 5.1.6 and LLM alignment in Appendix A, alongside additions such as RewardBench, WARM, and SRPO. These are substantive additions beyond bibliographic publication updates. The earlier comparison with prior surveys is preserved in Appendix B.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and concluding discussion receive substantial rewriting. Prior surveys move from Section 1.4 to Appendix B, Appendix A organizes LLM-specific explanations, and Section 9 gains three subsections. Numerous explanatory examples and language corrections are added, and a visible draft editing note in Section 3.2.2 is removed.

P2.justification: The seven tables and five schematic figures are retained with limited formatting, caption, and notation refinements. v2 Tables 2-3 move to Appendix B as v3 Tables 6-7, while the theoretical tables become Tables 4-5. Figure 1 also receives small label and text-contrast adjustments.

improvement.justification: The mathematical corrections, explicit DPO explanation, and LLM applicability discussion improve clarity and practical usefulness. Editorial cleanup also removes a visible draft note. These gains outweigh the small loss of the explicit trajectory-segment definition, while the central survey and theoretical tables remain largely unchanged.
